Jules Verne, The Mysterious Island, translated by Stephen W. White.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/jules-verne/the-mysterious-island/stephen-w-white

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Jules Verne, the author, died 1905 (Wikidata Q33977, P570 = 1905-03-24).
- Stephen W. White, the translator, died 1914 (Wikidata Q3498682, P570 = 1914-10-01).

First publication of the text used: 1876 (SE colophon: 'The Mysterious Island was published in 1874 by Jules Verne. It was translated from French in 1876 by Stephen W. White.'). The country of this translation's first publication is not stated in the facts.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1876, before 1931, so the United States public domain applies to it.
- Country of origin: the last person to die, Jules Verne, died in 1905, and Stephen W. White died in 1914. Every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever the country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
